edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Occupational lead exposure crosses the blood-brain barrier, interferes with calcium-dependent neurotransmission, and accelerates neuronal oxidative injury, all of which can erode cognition over time.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2021 Yu cohort in Scand J Work Environ Health, which ties occupational lead exposure to cognitive function in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
